quarterly_data.signal: President Pei-Ing Lee on the Q3 2026 call: net sales rose 61.9% QoQ and 611.7% YoY, mostly due to ASP up greater than 60% QoQ (greater than 500% YoY), primarily reflecting renewed long-term agreements; shipments decreased by mid-single digit due to depleted inventory and exchange rate was favorable by low single digit. Gross margin 85.7%, operating income TWD 106.8 billion at 80%, net income TWD 87.6 billion at a 65.6% net margin, EPS TWD 25.4; Q1-Q3 net profit TWD 163.9 billion (EPS TWD 49.28). SG&A rose to TWD 2.443 billion and R&D to TWD 5.145 billion, mainly due to concurrent and future employee compensation.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales +61.9% QoQ, +611.7% YoY; gross margin 85.7%; operating margin 80%; EPS TWD 25.4

quarterly_data.signal: Asked how much of the greater-than-60% QoQ ASP increase came from renewed long-term agreements, President Lee said it was a mix including renewals of one-year or 6-month LTAs mostly negotiated in the first, second or third quarter of last year when ASP was relatively low (Nanya fulfilled all deliveries at those agreed prices and most of those LTAs expired by Q3), plus Q2 and Q3 quarterly price updates; he could not quantify precisely but said 'more than half' came from the renewed long-term agreements.
quarterly_data.figure: more than half of the >60% QoQ ASP increase from renewed long-term agreements

quarterly_data.signal: President Lee on contract coverage: Nanya's current LTA coverage is around 50%-70%, with terms ranging from quarterly to three-year contracts; three-year contracts are more than 20% of output, and Nanya plans to increase long-term contracts according to customer demand ('Customer is very proactive in terms of getting longer term supply'). Floor and ceiling prices are being discussed for upcoming new contracts, with liability on both sides: Nanya commits capex, capacity growth and equipment purchases, customers commit to some degree to secure long-term supply. Fulfillment of signed long-term orders is maintained at 100%, while fulfillment of other supply inquiries is usually quite low.
quarterly_data.figure: LTA around 50%-70%; three-year contracts more than 20% of output; 100% fulfillment of signed long-term orders

quarterly_data.signal: President Lee: the AI infrastructure and server business (more than 20% of revenue) is a mix of DDR4, DDR5 and low-power DDR, chips used for communication, storage and system management, enterprise SSD and RDIMM. Nanya plans to increase that percentage through 2027, 2028 and 2029, targeting 40%-50% of revenue by 2029 or 2030, with the planned capacity (30K by end of 2028, 50K by end of 2030) including AI infrastructure. Products for the private-placement customers could include enterprise SSD, KV cache or high bandwidth flash, and communication, switch and management chips.
quarterly_data.figure: AI infrastructure target 40%-50% of revenue by 2029 or 2030 (currently more than 20%)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 product mix (President Lee): DDR5 remains around 10%; DDR4 and low-power DDR4 combined more than 60% (not including DDR3); other applications include low-power products for automotive, industrial and general consumer, plus PC (mostly DDR5). Lee: DDR4 demand is still quite strong - DDR4 alone is probably almost over 12%-14% of today's demand, and in 2025, when the industry started to end-of-life DDR4 and LPDDR4, the two combined were still almost 30% of market demand - versus Nanya's low-single-digit overall market share; DDR4/LPDDR4 demand will likely continue to get smaller but remaining demand is still quite strong compared to supply, and Nanya is flexible to shift DDR4 to DDR5 and other products.
quarterly_data.figure: DDR5 around 10%; DDR4 + LPDDR4 more than 60%; DDR4 12%-14% of market demand

quarterly_data.signal: President Lee: around 20% of Nanya's shipments are high-quality known good die wafers that customers dice directly into their multi-chip packages; the remaining 80% are devices or modules.
quarterly_data.figure: around 20% known good die wafers; 80% devices or modules

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Apple: President Lee said Nanya does not supply Apple's major DRAM but 'may have supplied' Apple's modem DRAM, a specialty DRAM for which he does not think other suppliers provide supply to Apple.

President Lee: more than one customer is working with Nanya on AI-related wafer-to-wafer bonding / 3DIC projects (he declined to comment on specific customers, citing confidentiality), with applications likely spanning cloud computation for AI to edge computation and physical AI; 'We already have some revenue. Not big, but it is an important business for Nanya to work on.'

President Lee: new-fab capex could go up to $16 billion (US dollars) just for one fab, for 50K, including construction, clean room, equipment and some EUV for the future; Nanya will balance this capex requirement against its dividend policy.

President Lee on the planned Pingtung Science Park 3D wafer packaging and test fab (mainly for wafer-to-wafer production): capex planning is not finalized but will likely be up to $10 billion in total in the long run; equipment move-in is targeted for second half 2028; the plan is mainly for customer demand on AI applications. Wafer-level processing will mostly be done by Nanya Technology, while FATC handles the back-end wafer assembly and test (grinding, dicing, packaging, assembly, testing).
quarterly_data.figure: up to $10 billion capex in the long run; equipment move-in second half 2028

quarterly_data.signal: President Lee's market view: the shortage is expected to continue in the December quarter with ASP likely improving gradually; next year likely remains tight because new capacity, construction and equipment delivery take long lead times, so a near-term solution is unlikely, especially in 2027 or early 2028; HBM negotiations for next year are about to be completed and HBM pricing may change capacity distribution. Nanya's own analysis of DRAM silicon area for AI chips suggests the shortage will persist for a long time, especially for AI, with the key index being whether the return on AI investment (US CSPs, LLM developers including Anthropic and OpenAI, and Mainland China) is sustainable. On whether double-digit contract price growth with gross margin around 80% can be sustained: 'This potentially possible.' Nanya's bit shipments will likely remain flat for a few quarters until second half of 2027, with no big growth in the beginning of 2027, given very depleted inventory.

President Lee on input costs: Nanya has multiple wafer suppliers, including its sister company; costs across the supply side - equipment, material, construction and labor, not just wafers - have increased, with some impact on cost balanced by higher DRAM ASP.
